text: Today we're covering the basics of nutrition, starting with the three macronutrients your body needs in large amounts: carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.
Carbohydrates are your body's main energy source. They get broken down into glucose, which your cells burn for fuel, and any extra is stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen.
Protein is mostly used for building and repairing tissue. It's made of amino acids, and your body needs a mix of them to build muscle, enzymes, and hormones.
Fats often get a bad reputation, but they're essential for absorbing certain vitamins, protecting your organs, and providing a concentrated, long-lasting source of energy.
Beyond macronutrients, your body also needs micronutrients in small amounts: vitamins and minerals like vitamin C, iron, and calcium, each supporting a different bodily function.
Staying hydrated matters just as much. Water regulates body temperature, helps transport nutrients, and is involved in nearly every chemical reaction inside your cells.
A common mistake is focusing on a single nutrient in isolation. What actually matters most for long-term health is the overall balance and variety across your whole diet.
